successors.note: Page silent: the infobox says 'Succeeded by: Delhi Sultanate' (the footer lists the Mamluk dynasty) and the last recorded event is 1294; the Shamsuddin Firoz Shah page has Sonargaon in his kingdom (reign 1301-1322). The balbani dossier takes the Dhaka country in 1301 (its ledger 2, counterpart this slug), so 1295-1300 is a gap in the sources. capitals.name: Bikrampur (Vikramapura)
capitals.note: 'The capital of the dynasty was Bikrampur in present-day Munshiganj District of Bangladesh.' The page says Dasharathadeva 'extended his kingdom up to Bikrampur and made it his capital' without a year; 1280 is a bridge before the alliance with Balban of 1281 (Danuj Rai 'of Sonargaon'). The seat of Purushottamadeva, Madhumathana and Damodaradeva before that is not on any page opened (Banglapedia's Deva Dynasty article covers only the 8th-9th century Buddhist Devas). 'His brother Bikramaditya Deva later moved to the eastern side of the kingdom in 1294'; the page names no city for the move.

'A later ruler of this dynasty Ariraja-Danuja-Madhava Dasharathadeva extended his kingdom up to Bikrampur and made it his capital' (no year); Danuj Rai 'of Sonargaon' made an alliance with Balban in 1281, so 1280 is a bridge year. WHICH SIDE HOLDS WESTERN DHAKA: from 1280 this dossier holds the Bikrampur disc to 1294; 11 of its 17 cells lie inside the Mamluk Dynasty shapes of 1236-1285 (keyframes 8-11 of mamluk-dynasty) and the balbani-sultanate-of-bengal 1287 shape (its keyframe 0, the Mamluk 1285 shape clipped to Bengal), 54 cells of the Dhaka division in all. The Deva page shows Balban allying with the local Hindu king, not governing Sonargaon (Yahya: 'he sought to enter into an alliance with the Hindu king of Eastern Bengal, Rai Danuj'), so the Cliopatria outline over-reaches there; mamluk-dynasty keyframes 8-11 (from 1280) and balbani keyframe 0 and ledger 0 should subtract the Dhaka 40 km disc until 1294. Not edited here.

region.text: the Deva kingdom of Damodaradeva: the Chittagong division (Comilla, Noakhali, Chittagong)

ledger.note: 1230: the Devas rule the Comilla-Noakhali-Chittagong country as the Sena kingdom ends. The infobox gives 'Established: 12th century', 'Preceded by: Sena dynasty'; 'Damodaradeva (reigned 1231-1243) was the most powerful ruler of this dynasty', with copperplates of 1234, 1236 and 1243; 'his kingdom was extended up to the present-day Comilla- Noakhali- Chittagong region'. The page dates no founding (Purushottamadeva, 'a village chief', and Madhumathana, 'the first independent ruler', are undated) and Banglapedia's Deva Dynasty article, opened 2026-11-01, covers only the Buddhist Devas; 1230 is the sena-dynasty dossier's disestablishment year, a bridge at confidence 1. The sena-dynasty ledger hands over 366 cells; the Chittagong division is the 98 the page supports.

This is the last recorded history of this dynasty.' The infobox says 'Disestablished: 13th century' and 'Succeeded by: Delhi Sultanate'; 1294 is a bridge. Ghiyas-ud-Din Balban allied with the Devas in 1281. Thin on 2026-11-01: Banglapedia's Deva Dynasty article covers only the Buddhist Devas of Devaparvata, so it does not date the end or place the eastern remnant; 1294 stays a bridge at confidence 1, and the balbani dossier's 1301 gain from this slug leaves 1295-1300 unexplained.

notes: No Cliopatria row. REPAIR of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a, verdict fail): (1) the Dhaka division and Bikrampur were drawn from 1230, but the Deva page brings Bikrampur in only under Dasharathadeva (undated; Damodaradeva's kingdom reached 'the present-day Comilla- Noakhali- Chittagong region'): 1230-1279 is now the Chittagong division (98 cells) and Bikrampur, Sonargaon and Dhaka (a 40 km disc round Dhaka) are a 1280 gain at confidence 1, a bridge before the alliance with Balban of 1281; the capital Bikrampur starts in 1280 and the earlier seat is unknown. (2) The double claim with mamluk-dynasty and balbani: the Chittagong division touches neither; the Bikrampur disc (17 cells, 11 of them in the Mamluk 1236-1285 shapes) is held HERE from 1280 to 1294 and by mamluk-dynasty (Cliopatria outline) before 1280. OPEN FOR OTHER DOSSIERS (not edited here): mamluk-dynasty keyframes 8-11 and balbani-sultanate-of-bengal keyframe 0 / ledger 0 should subtract the Dhaka 40 km disc from 1280 to 1294; mamluk-dynasty ledger 35 (1287 loss) counterpart should be balbani-sultanate-of-bengal; balbani ledger 2 (1301 gain from this slug) leaves 1295-1300 without an owner, so either balbani counterpart becomes 'nobody' or this dossier ends later. TWO DEVA DYNASTIES: the sena-dynasty dossier's 'deva-dynasty' (1230) is this 13th-century dynasty (Wikipedia 'Deva dynasty'); the khadga-dynasty dossier's 'deva-dynasty' (716) is the Buddhist dynasty written as first-deva-dynasty; khadga-dynasty successors and its 716 dissolve counterpart should be re-pointed there. START AND END: both are bridges (confidence 1): the page gives the infobox's 'Established 12th century' and 'Disestablished 13th century', Damodaradeva's reign from 1231 and a last record in 1294; Banglapedia (opened 2026-11-01) is silent on these Devas; the Sena page says Lakshmana Sena's descendants 'ruled in Bengal (Bang) till at least 1245 AD or 1260 AD', so Sena and Deva overlap in the same country for a generation. AFTER 1294: the eastern remnant (Bikramaditya's 'eastern side of the kingdom') is unplaced; Chittagong was conquered by Fakhruddin in 1340 (Bengal Sultanate page, via the balbani dossier). RULERS: only Damodaradeva (1231-1243) has years; no ruler strip. Gazetteer names needed: Bikrampur (place; regions here use Dhaka 40 km).
